request.tone: quiet persistence and civic stakes; scariness mild, peril mild, violence none
request.note: catalog book read blind; no request exists

pitch.hero: Jonah, twelve, whose grandmother Ada has kept the orchard's daily notebooks for sixty years
pitch.want: to prove the old orchard is of scientific interest and stop a road through the Bramley row
pitch.obstacle: a thin August survey, a six-week objection window, and a record that is only proof with a method
pitch.stake: eighty-two homes and a spine road through the orchard, and trust lost if he claims what he cannot show
pitch.ending_kind: branch and bottleneck: shortcuts and blame end early; careful evidence wins a fair hearing

jonah.name: Jonah
jonah.want: to prove the orchard matters before the objection window closes
jonah.voice: third person past; watchful, stubborn, learning to say only what he can prove

ada.name: Ada
ada.role: keeper of the orchard notebooks, eighty-one, Jonah's grandmother
ada.want: to keep the record as a record, not a weapon
ada.voice: few words, dry and exact; refuses to claim what she cannot show

tobe.name: Tobe
tobe.role: friend; runs the school weather club
tobe.want: to turn a century of bloom dates into solid numbers
tobe.voice: eager, practical, thorough to the point of frightening

mrs_cassar.name: Mrs Cassar
mrs_cassar.role: beekeeper with thirty years of hive records
mrs_cassar.want: never to have her rough counts dressed up as exact
mrs_cassar.voice: blunt, honest, kind in practical ways

okonkwo.name: Mrs Okonkwo
okonkwo.role: city archivist at the Tuesday desk
okonkwo.want: records kept safe and their custody proven

abara.name: Dr Ines Abara
abara.want: evidence whose method can be shown
abara.voice: slow, careful, says only what she can defend

raval.name: Priya Raval
raval.want: data with a method, a named keeper and a way to check
raval.voice: plain, busy, careful with the line she may not cross

faulks.name: D. Faulks
faulks.want: unstated; defends his method at the hearing

halvor.name: Halvor
halvor.want: to learn what would make Jonah stop
halvor.voice: polite, fair, honest in a way that is hard to answer

carver.name: Carver
carver.want: to run the story when Jonah chooses

truth.question: Is the old orchard really of no particular scientific interest?
truth.statement: No. The survey that called the site of no particular scientific interest rested on four short visits in the driest days of a dry August. The shed's hundred and fourteen years of notebooks, copied, checked and kept with a stated method, show the bloom moving about eleven days earlier across the century, and that careful record, not the single October bloom, is the evidence that forces a proper hearing and resurvey.

late_october.text: It is the last week of October when the story opens.

bramley_top_of_hill.text: A big old Bramley apple tree stands at the top of the orchard hill.

bramley_october_bloom.text: The big Bramley is covered in white blossom in late October, as if it were May.

other_trees_bare.text: Every other tree on the slope is bare.

jonah.text: Jonah is the boy at the centre of the story, who lives by the orchard hill.

ada_daily_notebook.text: Ada writes the day up in a ruled notebook in the shed every evening, and has since before Jonah was born.

shed_heater.text: The shed has a ticking paraffin heater and smells of old paper.

ada_already_knew.text: Ada already knew about the October blossom and was not surprised.

hives_on_orchard.text: There are beehives in the orchard, along the south fence.

notice_on_gate.text: A notice has been put up on the orchard gate.

jonah_asked_notebooks.text: Jonah asked Ada whether the notebooks had recorded an October blossom before.

jonah_went_to_notice.text: Jonah went down to the gate to read the notice.

jonah_sought_author.text: Jonah set out to find who wrote the survey.

no_prior_october_bloom.text: No earlier October in the notebooks has a blossom like this one.

loose_sheet_1952.text: A loose sheet in the back of the 1952 notebook is a list by Ada's mother of every strange thing the orchard has done.

mother_list_details.text: Ada's mother's list includes a bloom in November 1948 and a frost in June 1953.

odd_events_pattern.text: Dr Abara agrees that a recorded pattern of odd events is itself evidence.

oddities_cluster.text: The oddities on the 1952 list bunch in years with a mild winter or a late spring.

bees_out_in_october.text: The bees are out and working in late October, tricked by the blossom's warmth.

mrs_cassar_beekeeper.text: Mrs Cassar keeps bees by the orchard and has done for thirty years.

cassar_never_seen.text: Mrs Cassar has never seen bees work like this in the last week before the frosts.

cassar_spiral_records.text: Mrs Cassar keeps her own hive records in spiral notebooks.

bee_count_mismatch.text: Mrs Cassar counted 240 foraging bees and Jonah fewer than half; the gap never closed.

notice_is_survey_summary.text: The notice on the gate is an early ecological survey summary, typed and official.

notice_appeared_today.text: The notice appeared on the gate that same day, since the morning.

jonah_photo_of_notice.text: Jonah has a photo of the notice in place on the gate, with the bare trees behind it.

photo_only_record.text: Jonah's photo turns out to be the only picture anyone has of the notice in place.

notice_zip_tied.text: The notice is fastened to the gate with zip-ties.

notice_later_removed.text: The notice is later taken down, and nobody can say exactly what it said or when it appeared.

notice_posted_late.text: The photo's date stamp shows the notice went up only in October, cutting the objection window short.

notebooks_six_shelves.text: The orchard notebooks fill six shelves on the shed wall.

notebooks_1911_to_now.text: The notebooks run from 1911 to the present.

record_114_years.text: The notebooks hold a hundred and fourteen years of records.

nine_hands.text: Nine different people have written in the notebooks over the years.

several_hands.text: The notebooks are written in several different handwritings.

notebooks_no_index.text: The notebooks have no index, list or key.

notebooks_contents.text: The notebooks record weather, blossom, frost, picking weights, wasp years and prices such as ladders.

eight_named_hands.text: Ada can name eight of the nine hands.

ninth_hand_unknown.text: The ninth hand, a small neat pencil from 1939 to 1943, is unknown even to Ada.

shed_one_bulb.text: The shed is lit by a single bulb on a wire.

ada_doubts_notebooks.text: Ada says the notebooks are only weather and does not believe they can change anything.

ada_sixty_years.text: Ada has written the day up every evening for sixty years.

ada_since_21.text: Ada began writing the day up at twenty-one because her mother and grandmother did it before her.

ada_weapon_unease.text: Ada is uneasy about the notebooks being used as a weapon.

notebooks_never_left_shed.text: Ada has never let a notebook leave the shed in sixty years.

notebook_at_archive.text: The first notebook volume is laid out on the city archive's desk.

first_entry_1911.text: The first volume opens in March 1911 with the price of ladders and a first bloom date of 14 April.

hard_1920s_hand.text: The 1920s handwriting is hard to read; a three and a five look almost the same.

unreadable_figures.text: Some figures in the notebooks cannot be read with certainty.

missing_years.text: Some years are missing from the notebook record.

missing_1917_1918.text: The 1917 and 1918 notebook volumes are missing from the shelf.

record_unbroken.text: The notebooks are described as a long unbroken local series.

other_buildings.text: Besides the shed, the hill has an old packing shed, a stone bothy and a garage loft.

four_periods.text: The nine hands sort into four periods of writing.

ada_father_shop.text: Ada's father kept an accounts book in his shop.

ada_father_contract.text: Ada's father once signed a contract that lost him half the hill.

horse_story.text: Ada's gran said the army took the farm horse in 1917 and brought it back in 1919.

survey_exists.text: An ecological survey of the orchard site has been written.

survey_signed_faulks.text: The survey is signed D. Faulks.

survey_dated_august.text: The survey is dated in August.

faulks_name_in_book.text: Jonah has written the name D. Faulks in the back of his exercise book.

survey_no_interest.text: The survey's key sentence says the site is of no particular scientific interest.

sentence_eleven_words.text: The survey's key sentence is eleven words long.

exercise_book_eleven_words.text: Jonah has copied the survey's eleven words into the back of an exercise book.

august_orchard_looks_empty.text: In August the orchard looks like nothing much: long grass, shade and a duckweed pond.

survey_four_visits.text: The survey method lists four short site visits in August, all dry, none longer than an hour.

survey_under_four_hours.text: The survey visits add up to just under four hours in total.

one_error_enough.text: One wrong date would be enough for Faulks to throw out the whole set.

survey_data_thin.text: The survey's raw data is thin: four visits, one line across the slope, and twenty-two plant species.

survey_site_dry.text: The survey data notes that the site was dry at the time of the survey.

survey_driest_days.text: Public rain records show the four survey visits fell in the driest days of that August.

rainfall_record.text: Public Met Office rainfall records for that August can be checked.

august_driest.text: The survey's August was the driest month of a dry year.

faulks_pattern.text: Faulks's other reports formed a pattern of always matching what the client wanted.

faulks_timing.text: At the hearing Faulks says his method was sound but the timing, a dry August, was unlucky.

orchard_pond.text: The orchard has a pond at the bottom of the hill.

tree_count_unsteady.text: Jonah's count of the orchard trees comes out differently each time.

developer_exists.text: A developer plans to build on the orchard.

development_82_homes.text: The development plan is eighty-two homes and a spine road.

road_through_bramley_row.text: The planned spine road runs straight along the row where the big Bramley stands.

frost_pocket.text: There is a frost pocket in the low ground by the pond where cold air settles.

bramley_above_frost.text: The big Bramley stands just above the frost line, in ground that never freezes as hard.

tobe_known.text: Tobe runs the school weather club and helps Jonah with the numbers.

tobe_laptop.text: Tobe has a working laptop that the project uses for typing and charts.

city_archive.text: The city archive keeps a Tuesday desk for people bringing in old records.

okonkwo_archivist.text: Mrs Okonkwo is the archivist at the city archive.

abara.text: Dr Ines Abara is a university scientist who works on long-term monitoring.

raval.text: Priya Raval is the council's ecology officer.

halvor.text: Halvor is a young, polite representative of the developer.

carver_editor.text: Carver, the local paper's editor of thirty years, will run the story when Jonah chooses.

writers_family.text: Four of the nine writers have living family in the city.

window_six_weeks.text: Objections to the development close six weeks after the notice.

form_needs_proof.text: The council objection form asks for proof of scientific interest, the same phrase the survey used.

school_class.text: Jonah's school class could help with the typing.

forty_thousand_lines.text: Typing everything would mean about forty thousand daily lines.

four_lines_plan.text: The plan is to type only four key dates a year, 456 numbers in all, instead of everything.

four_lines_bloom_frost.text: The four lines a year are bloom dates and frost dates.

four_dates_with_picking.text: The four dates are first bloom, full bloom, last frost and first picking.

archive_checks_in_person.text: The archive will not take anything it cannot see and check in person.

school_hall_thursdays.text: The school hall is free on Thursdays and the caretaker agreed to lend it.

photo_every_page.text: Tobe's rule is to photograph every typed page so anyone can check a number.

spreadsheet.text: Tobe has set up a spreadsheet for the dates.

bloom_chart.text: Tobe has made a chart of bloom dates against years.

bloom_eleven_days.text: Across the century the bloom dates moved about eleven days earlier.

cassar_hive_30_years.text: Mrs Cassar has thirty years of hive records and will share them.

cassar_method_changes.text: Mrs Cassar changed her counting method in 2005 and again in 2014.

archive_offer.text: Mrs Okonkwo offered a locked, temperature-stable archive shelf for the notebooks, with Ada free to visit.

cassar_carrier_bags.text: Mrs Cassar has brought her hive records in two carrier bags.

needs_method.text: The record counts as evidence only if it can be shown how it was measured and by whom.

double_typing.text: Every page is typed by two people and compared; the first hundred pages had eleven mismatches.

unclear_marked.text: Unclear figures are marked with a question mark and listed: nineteen of 456.

cassar_no_pretending.text: Mrs Cassar insists her early counts were rough and must not be presented as exact.

abara_visit.text: Dr Abara has walked the orchard rows in the rain.

local_paper.text: There is a local newspaper that could cover the orchard story.

newspaper_offer.text: The local paper has offered to run a story with a photo of Ada and the notebooks.

class_typed_1930s.text: Thirty people typed up the 1930s notebooks in the school hall on Thursdays.

raval_not_ready.text: Raval says the notebooks are not proof yet: they need a method, a chain of care and a way to check.

chart_on_door.text: The printed bloom chart is pinned to the shed door.

council_corridor_wait.text: Jonah waited forty minutes in a council corridor by a recycling poster.

custody_note.text: Mrs Okonkwo writes a custody note recording where every volume has been.

raval_three_things.text: Raval can accept a data set with a stated method, a named keeper and a way for anyone to check it.

abara_cold_air.text: Dr Abara will write two pages on cold air drainage if six weeks of dawn readings are taken.

dawn_readings.text: Thermometer readings are taken at dawn for the frost pocket study.

cassar_three_blocks.text: Mrs Cassar's dated method changes split her records into three clean blocks.

four_objections.text: Tobe listed four objections Faulks could make: not continuous, untrained observers, inconsistent method, unchecked.

data_request.text: Jonah has formally requested the survey's raw data, due within twenty working days.

jonah_signed_hall.text: Jonah signed to book the school hall for the rest of term.

thermometers_two.text: Two thermometers are read at dawn, one in the frost pocket and one at the top of the hill.

one_thermometer.text: Until a second one was bought, the frost study relied on a single thermometer.

frost_four_degrees.text: The frost pocket is up to four degrees colder than the top of the hill.

blue_notebook.text: The dawn readings go into a new notebook with a blue cover.

method_section.text: Jonah writes the method section explaining how the notebooks were kept, copied, checked and stored.

method_why.text: Dr Abara sent Jonah's first method draft back with one word: why.

four_letters.text: Jonah has written letters to the families of four of the writers.

plaque_offer.text: The developer offers a saved corner, a sign and a plaque with Ada's name, but not the Bramley row.

parish_records.text: The parish records are kept at the same city archive.

tobe_readings.text: Tobe did nineteen of the forty-two dawn readings.

halvor_question.text: Halvor asked Jonah what would make him stop.

halvor_coffee.text: Halvor bought Jonah a coffee he did not drink.

species_36.text: Ada added fourteen species from memory, making thirty-six, unconfirmed until spring.

receipt_1917.text: A parish receipt records two orchard books lent to the farming board in August 1917, marked not returned.

board_basement.text: The farming board's successor keeps an office with a basement in the old market building.

card_index.text: The basement has a card index that stops in 1961, under a light on a four-minute timer.

now_november.text: It is now November and the orchard is asleep.

spring_survey_needed.text: A proper species list needs a trained surveyor walking the rows in May.

nine_species_sure.text: Jonah can be sure of only nine species in November.

volumes_found.text: The missing war-years volumes are found in a box marked WAR COMMITTEE MISC in the basement.

found_both_1917.text: The two recovered books are both 1917 volumes.

orchard_trust.text: The Orchard Hill Trust is set up with three signatures: Ada, Mrs Cassar and Jonah's mother.

objection_submitted.text: The objection went in with the data, the method, the custody note and a new covering sentence.

hearing.text: There will be a council hearing on the objection.

hearing_public.text: The hearing is held in public.

cassar_frame.text: Mrs Cassar has a perfect honeycomb frame in a glass case, kept since 2008.

frost_chart.text: There is a chart of the frost pocket readings beside the bloom chart.

page_1947.text: Ada read a March 1947 page about a cold snap that blackened the early blossom.

officer_report.text: The officer's report drops the no-interest wording and cites the long records, frost data and species list.

three_conditions.text: Conditions require a May resurvey by a fresh ecologist, a full-winter frost study and the records lodged with the archive.

road_could_move.text: The report says the spine road could be moved forty metres east, at a price.

rota.text: A rota of names on the shed door keeps the dawn readings going.

resurvey_61.text: The May resurvey found sixty-one species, including an orchid never recorded on the hill.

war_volume_horse_line.text: A September 1917 line in the recovered volumes records the horse as taken and given back.

window_closed_unused.text: The objection window closed without the notebooks being used.

typed_twelve_years.text: Trying to type everything, Jonah finished only twelve years before the deadline crushed him.

notebooks_archived.text: The notebooks are placed in the archive's temperature-stable room.

chart_sent_unchecked.text: The chart was sent round before it was checked, and a correction harmed trust in Jonah.

chart_sent_alone.text: The chart was sent alone, without method or custody papers, and was admired and filed.

three_guesses_wrong.text: Faulks found three guessed dates wrong, and the whole set was treated as guesses.

paper_photo_ran.text: The paper ran a photo of Ada with the notebooks on page five, and the deadline passed.

jonah_accused_faulks.text: Jonah said publicly that Faulks shaped the survey for the builder, which he could not prove.

file_online_unanswered.text: The unchecked file went online, was read by four hundred people, and was never used officially.

numbers_returned.text: Raval returned the numbers because they came without a stated method.

volumes_kept_secret.text: Jonah returned the found volumes to the shed without telling anyone where they had been.

dossier_rushed.text: The deadline chose the release date and an incomplete dossier went in.

objection_accepted.text: The objection was accepted on its evidence and the survey ordered redone in May.

copy_lodged.text: The finished copy of the record was lodged with the archive, open to anyone.

decision_against.text: The panel decided against the orchard after Jonah argued with the chair.

six_answers.text: Jonah answered six questions with evidence and one honestly as unknown, and a new survey was ordered.

deed_of_gift.text: The notebooks went to the archive by deed of gift, with Ada free to read them.

road_moved.text: The road was moved forty metres east and the Bramley row still stands.

abara_attention.text: Dr Abara says one October bloom proves nothing, but a century of dates proves a great deal.

jonah_continues.text: Jonah takes up writing the day in the record in his own hand.

ada_new_notebook.text: Ada is still writing in the new notebook months after the bloom.

record_closed.text: Nobody added to the notebooks after Ada's entry on the evening of the October bloom.

eleven_day_gap.text: The winter readings stopped for eleven days over Christmas, leaving a gap.

orchard_watched.text: The orchard is watched and the series is public and growing.

first_index.text: Jonah made the first index of the six shelves.

spring_normal_bloom.text: In April the Bramley row blossomed normally and the October bloom did not recur.

next_october_no_bloom.text: The next October the Bramley did not bloom and the picking was normal.

argument_cost.text: The fight strained two friendships and left Ada more tired.

new_eleven_words.text: Jonah's covering sentence says the site is of long-term scientific interest, evidenced by the record.

n00c0.event: In the last week of October Jonah finds the big Bramley at the top of the hill in full white blossom while every other tree is bare.

n01d0.event: Jonah tells Ada in the shed about the blossom; she says only that she knows, and three paths open.

n02c0.event: Ada searches decades of notebooks and finds no October bloom like it, but Jonah spots her mother's loose list of strange events in the 1952 book.

n02c1.event: The hives along the south fence hum in October; Mrs Cassar says she has never seen bees do this in thirty years.

n02c2.event: Jonah reads a new survey summary notice tied to the orchard gate and photographs it, the only picture ever taken of it in place.

n03d0.event: Jonah faces six shelves of notebooks from 1911, nine hands and no index, and must choose where to start.

cq_plant_did_find_who_wrote.event: Jonah finds the survey signed D. Faulks in August and writes the name in the back of his exercise book.

n03d1.event: Jonah and Mrs Cassar compare bee counts at her kitchen table and the gap between them will not close.

n03d2.event: At the gate Jonah reads the survey's eleven-word sentence calling the site of no particular scientific interest.

n04d0.event: Jonah studies the D. Faulks signature and thinks about how empty an orchard looks in August.

n04d1.event: The survey's method section shows four short dry visits in August, about four hours behind eleven words.

n04d2.event: Ada says the notebooks are only weather and cannot change anything; Jonah cannot prove her wrong.

n04c0.event: At the kitchen table Jonah copies the eleven words into the back of an exercise book and pockets it.

n04c1.event: Under the shed's single swinging bulb Jonah runs a finger along the oldest grey notebooks.

n04c2.event: Jonah walks the rows counting trees, loses count at the pond, and gets a different number the second time.

n04c3.event: Ada tells Jonah she can name eight of the nine hands; the ninth, a pencil from 1939 to 1943, is a mystery.

n04c4.event: Jonah photographs the zip-tied notice; later that photo is the only record of the notice in place.

n05d0.event: Objections close in six weeks and the council form demands proof of scientific interest, the survey's own phrase.

n05d1.event: The survey visits total under four hours, yet the sentence could bring eighty-two houses and a road through the Bramley row.

n05d2.event: Mrs Okonkwo at the city archive's Tuesday desk hears Jonah out and asks to see what he has.

n05d3.event: Jonah finds Dr Ines Abara, a long-term monitoring scientist who might understand the notebooks.

n05d4.event: The developer's brochure shows eighty-two homes and a spine road running exactly along the Bramley's row.

n05d5.event: Tobe, of the school weather club, is thrilled by a century of bloom dates and opens his laptop.

e05_0.event: The six weeks pass in ordinary days; Jonah is left with a photo, the eleven copied words and what he did not do.

n06d0.event: Tobe estimates forty thousand daily lines, far too many for six weeks.

n06d1.event: Tobe proposes typing four lines a year, bloom and frost dates, 456 numbers in all.

n06d2.event: The faded, slanting 1920s hand makes digits ambiguous, and one wrong week could hand Faulks the whole set.

n06d3.event: Ada will not let notebooks leave the shed and the archive will not take what it cannot check, so the notebooks stay put.

cq_payoff_did_go_down_read.event: Jonah's date-stamped photo of the zip-tied notice shows it went up only in October, cutting the window short.

n06d4.event: The shed has one socket and Ada will not have the books in the house, so the school hall on Thursdays is offered.

n06d5.event: Tobe insists every typed page be photographed so any number can be checked.

n06c0.event: On the archive desk the 1911 volume opens with the price of ladders and a first bloom date of 14 April.

n06c1.event: The laptop runs off an extension lead on the shed bench while Ada reads the first line aloud.

n06c2.event: Jonah sets up the laptop and the first notebook on a folding table by the orchard pond.

n06c3.event: Ada reads the 1920s pages aloud while Jonah types, her voice slowing on remembered dates.

n06c4.event: Jonah's test photos of a page improve until he has a system.

n06c5.event: There are no 1917 or 1918 volumes and no note of where they went.

n06c6.event: Eating toast late at night, Jonah hears Ada say this is what the work mostly is.

e06_0.event: Trying to type every line, Jonah completes twelve years before the task crushes him.

n07d0.event: Four dates a year, 456 numbers: Tobe sets up a spreadsheet of four columns and 114 rows.

n07d1.event: Jonah weighs making the case on the Bramley row alone, simple enough for one sentence.

n07d2.event: Mrs Cassar offers thirty years of hive records but insists her method changed in 2005 and 2014.

n07d3.event: Mrs Okonkwo offers a locked, stable archive shelf with a receipt and Ada's right to visit.

n07d4.event: Dr Abara says the long series is rare but is evidence only if its method can be shown.

n07d5.event: Tobe's chart shows the bloom dates creeping eleven days earlier across the century.

n07d6.event: Jonah imagines thirty typists in the school hall, fast but error-prone.

n07d7.event: Everyone knows one date out by a fortnight would let Faulks dismiss the chart.

n07d8.event: Ada says she never saw the notebooks as an argument and dislikes them becoming a weapon.

e07_0.event: The notebooks are safe in Mrs Okonkwo's stable archive room, but the window closes unused and the August survey is repeated.

e07_1.event: The unchecked chart spreads round the neighbourhood and a correction damages trust in Jonah.

n08d0.event: Two people type every page and Tobe's laptop finds eleven mismatches in the first hundred pages.

n08d1.event: Unclear figures are marked with a question mark and listed openly: nineteen of 456.

n08d2.event: Mrs Cassar brings two carrier bags of hive records and one rule: no pretending her counts are exact.

n08d3.event: Dr Abara walks the rows in the rain and asks whether anyone has measured the frost pocket.

cq_payoff_did_ask_whether_notebooks.event: Instead of blaming Faulks, Jonah shows Abara the 1952 list of odd events, and she agrees the pattern is evidence.

n08d4.event: Thirty people type in the Thursday hall and finish the 1930s by four o'clock.

n08d5.event: The 1917 and 1918 volumes are missing; they might be in the packing shed, the bothy or the garage loft.

n08d6.event: Priya Raval, the council ecology officer, says the notebooks are not proof yet.

n08c0.event: The printed bloom chart is pinned to the shed door and passers-by stop to look.

n08c1.event: At dawn the low ground by the pond is white with frost below the Bramley, and Jonah sees the orchard is many places.

n08c2.event: The nine hands sort into four periods, the changeovers unexplained in the record.

n08c3.event: Jonah waits forty minutes in a council corridor and writes his points for Raval on an envelope.

n08c4.event: Mrs Cassar carries the bag of 1990s hive notebooks up the hill herself.

n08c5.event: Tobe explains the spreadsheet to Ada as a ledger like her father's shop accounts, and she approves.

n08c6.event: Jonah stares at the smooth eleven-day drift in the chart and sees a story in it.

e08_0.event: Jonah sends the chart alone without method or custody note; it is admired and filed and the window closes.

e08_1.event: Faulks finds three guessed dates wrong and the whole chart is treated as guesses.

n09d0.event: Raval says she can accept data with a stated method, a named keeper and a way to check, which almost nobody brings.

n09d1.event: Dr Abara will write on cold air drainage only if six weeks of dawn readings are taken.

n09d2.event: Mrs Okonkwo will write a custody note tying each notebook to the archive and the orchard.

n09d3.event: Mrs Cassar dates her method changes, splitting her records into three clean blocks, the openness Raval asked for.

n09d4.event: Tobe lists the four objections Faulks would make, all of them fair.

n09d7.event: Ada recalls her gran's one war story: a horse taken by the army in 1917 and returned in 1919.

n09d8.event: Twelve-year-old Jonah signs to book the school hall for the rest of term.

e09_0.event: The paper runs a lovely photo of Ada on page five while the deadline passes and the road stays on the map.

e09_1.event: Jonah publicly claims the survey was made to order, cannot prove it, and loses trust.

n10d0.event: Two thermometers read at dawn for six weeks show the frost pocket up to four degrees colder.

n10d1.event: The formal data request gets a reference number and a polite reply promising data in twenty working days.

n10d2.event: Jonah writes the method section, the hardest writing of all.

n10d3.event: Jonah drafts letters to the living families of four of the nine writers.

cq_payoff_did_ask_whether_notebooks_site.event: With the 1952 list in mind, Jonah checks the survey visits and finds August was the driest month of a dry year.

n10d4.event: At the archive Mrs Okonkwo brings the parish record boxes that may explain the books lost in 1917.

n10d5.event: Carver, the paper's editor, will run the story whenever Jonah chooses; the photo of Ada is ready.

n10d6.event: The objection form has one name line, and putting eighty-one-year-old Ada's name there would be a burden.

n10c0.event: The dawn readings are dull and hard; Tobe does nineteen of the forty-two without complaint.

n10c1.event: Jonah waits on the data request: four weeks against a six-week window.

n10c2.event: Dr Abara returns Jonah's three-page method draft with one word: why.

n10c3.event: Jonah posts the four letters to the writers' families and waits.

n10c4.event: Mrs Okonkwo leaves Jonah alone with the 1917 parish box.

n10c5.event: The frost readings chart goes up on the shed door beside the bloom chart.

n10c6.event: Ada refuses to sign until the objection is ready, remembering her father's lost half of the hill.

e10_0.event: The whole unchecked file goes online and four hundred people read it, but nobody with power answers.

e10_1.event: The numbers go in without a method and Raval sends them back.

n11d0.event: The survey's raw data arrives: four visits, one line, twenty-two plants, and a note that the site was dry.

n11d1.event: Tobe shows from Met Office records that all four survey visits fell in the driest days of August.

cq_payoff_did_find_who_wrote_site2.event: Recalling the name D. Faulks from his exercise book, Jonah can ask Halvor whether the survey was timed for a dry August.

n11d2.event: Ada adds fourteen species from memory to the survey's twenty-two but will not swear to them until spring.

n11d3.event: The parish box holds a receipt for two orchard books lent to the farming board in 1917, never returned.

n11d4.event: Mrs Okonkwo traces the farming board to an office with a basement in the old market building.

n11d5.event: Jonah answers Tobe's four objections in writing; two are solid and two are not.

cq_payoff_did_find_who_wrote.event: Recalling Faulks's pattern of client-pleasing reports, Jonah lets the facts speak and sends the strengthened file.

n11d6.event: Dr Abara will read the dossier once and decide whether to put her name near it.

n11d7.event: Raval explains what the board will look for but not whether Jonah's file meets it.

n11d8.event: Halvor from the developer buys Jonah an untouched coffee and asks what would make him stop.

e11_0.event: The developer offers a saved corner and a plaque for Ada, but not the Bramley row; the rest becomes houses and a road.

e11_1.event: Jonah publishes his charge against Faulks and the fight becomes about him instead of the orchard.

n12d0.event: The visits, rain log and method together show the survey caught the site in its one dry spell.

n12d1.event: In the old market building's basement Jonah works through the 1917 card index under a four-minute light.

n12d2.event: It is November; a proper species list needs May, and Jonah's thirty-six names are only a first try.

n12d3.event: Jonah weighs telling Halvor honestly that nothing would make him stop.

n12d4.event: Six weeks of dawn readings show a steady gap of up to four degrees, a small but real data set.

n12d5.event: Jonah weighs asking eighty-one-year-old Ada to read her mother's page in a public room.

n12d6.event: Releasing the dossier early or late both carry costs; the deadline is marked in red.

n12c0.event: Jonah searches the card index in the old market basement, four minutes of light at a time.

n12c1.event: The Met Office rainfall record shows the survey days were the driest of the month.

n12c2.event: Walking the November rows, Jonah can be sure of only nine species.

n12c3.event: The coffee goes cold between Jonah and Halvor while Jonah gives careful answers.

n12c4.event: Ada says the hard part of speaking in rooms is the kindness afterwards.

n12c5.event: Every page of the dossier is numbered and sourced, which disposes of Tobe's four points.

n12c6.event: Jonah finds the two 1917 books in a WAR COMMITTEE MISC box in the basement, intact.

e12_0.event: Jonah quietly returns the found volumes to the shed and keeps their story to himself.

e12_1.event: The deadline picks the release and a rushed dossier goes in; the Faulks name stayed unused in Jonah's exercise book.

n13d0.event: The objection goes in with the data, method, custody note, nine sure species and a new covering sentence.

n13d1.event: The Orchard Hill Trust is set up so the objection comes from an organisation, not an old woman and a boy.

n13d2.event: A public hearing would make Faulks answer out loud, for better or worse.

n13d3.event: Ada and Tobe disagree about giving the developer the dossier before the hearing.

n13d4.event: The recovered war books go back into the record with their receipt, proving the record's care.

n13d5.event: Dr Abara will attend the hearing and say only what she can defend.

n13d6.event: Mrs Cassar will bring her hive counts and a perfect honeycomb frame in a glass case.

n13d7.event: Jonah weighs having Ada read one chosen page aloud at the hearing.

e13_0.event: The objection is accepted on its evidence and the survey must be redone in May.

e13_1.event: The copying is finished and lodged with the archive with Mrs Okonkwo's custody note; the record is safe.

e13_2.event: Reading the dossier, Jonah sees the notebooks are about nine hands showing up for 114 years.

n14d0.event: At the hearing Tobe's rainfall sheet answers why the survey should not stand in ninety seconds.

n14d1.event: Called amateur, Jonah answers with the custody note, the double-typing records and the marked doubts.

n14d2.event: Jonah admits the six weeks of frost data are short before anyone else can, and the panel respects it.

n14d3.event: Faulks says his method was sound but done in the wrong two dry weeks of August.

n14d4.event: Ada reads a March 1947 page about a cold snap and the room goes still.

n14d5.event: Jonah gives the file to the panel, the builder and the public on the same day.

n14c0.event: The hearing runs an hour late and Jonah's nerves burn off before the orchard item.

n14c1.event: The bloom and frost charts stand on an easel all afternoon before the orchard item is called.

n14c2.event: The note-taker writes Dr Abara's phrase long unbroken local series into the minutes.

n14c3.event: Mrs Cassar's honeycomb frame passes along the panel table.

n14c4.event: After Ada reads the 1947 page, the room is silent for eight seconds.

n14c5.event: Waiting again by the recycling poster, Mrs Cassar tells Jonah about a 1994 swarm.

e14_0.event: Jonah argues with a fair question, the chair turns careful, and the decision goes against the orchard.

e14_1.event: Jonah answers six questions with evidence and one honestly, and a new growing-season survey is ordered.

n15d0.event: The officer's report drops the no-interest wording and cites the records, frost data and species list.

n15d1.event: Three conditions set a May resurvey, a full-winter frost study and the records lodged with the archive.

n15d2.event: The report says the spine road could move forty metres east at a price, which might save the Bramley row.

n15d3.event: Jonah weighs whether the notebooks go to the archive, the trust or stay in the shed.

n15d4.event: Jonah writes the class an honest letter about the hearing and the road that might move.

n15d5.event: The readings matter only if someone keeps the rota on the shed door going every morning.

n15d6.event: Halvor asks again what would make Jonah stop, and now the answer is a fair process.

e15_0.event: The notebooks go to the archive by deed of gift, the war-years gap now a catalogue note of their recovery.

e15_1.event: The road moves forty metres east, the Bramley row stands, and the developer funds five years of checking.

e15_2.event: Dr Abara says the tree was not a signal but a question, answered by the attention in the notebooks.

n16d0.event: A full winter of readings needs nine people, a spare thermometer and someone to hold December, which will be Jonah.

n16d1.event: Ada teaches young volunteers to read the nine hands.

n16d2.event: After four meetings the trust's purpose is written down: something between a weapon and a home.

n16d3.event: Someone must write the day up every evening, as Ada has for sixty years.

n16c0.event: A second thermometer for eleven pounds keeps the frost study safe from a single failure.

n16c1.event: The rota goes up where the chart used to be and changes as people drop out and step in.

n16c2.event: The war volumes are ordinary, with one September 1917 line about the horse taken and given back.

n16c3.event: The May resurvey finds sixty-one species, including an orchid new to the hill.

e16_0.event: Jonah writes up the day in a new blue notebook in his own hand, starting the hundred and fifteenth year.

e16_1.event: The December readings stop for eleven days over Christmas, leaving a gap in the winter series.

n17d0.event: The resurvey report lists sixty-one species and advises the orchard be watched, not cleared.

n17d1.event: Four months on, the fight has strained friendships and tired Ada, whose writing is shakier in the new notebook.

n17d2.event: Jonah would keep all the work except the one thing he said about Faulks.

n17d3.event: In April the whole row blossoms normally and the October bloom does not recur.

e17_0.event: The orchard is watched and the record goes on, in the archive, the shed and Tobe's laptop.

e17_1.event: Jonah understands a record is not proof but the reason a person can be believed.

e18_0.event: Jonah spends a year making the first index of the six shelves; the road has moved and the study continues.

e18_1.event: The next October the Bramley does not bloom, the road runs forty metres east, and the picking is ordinary.

e18_2.event: Jonah rereads the eleven words in his exercise book; they were answered, not beaten.

e18_3.event: The notebooks sit closed in the archive; nobody added to them after the October bloom entry.
